data.why: The repo bundles demo/treino_demo.db, a small SQLite file of pre-labeled training cases (known brown-dwarf dwarfs, common stars, and Phase-3 rejects) built exactly for the offline training mode (app/demo.py), so no files need to be copied or synthesized.

goals: Decide, from the infrared cutout, whether there is a compact, reddish point source inside the crosshair or just noise/artifact
Check the optical cutout for a counterpart: nothing or a faint red point favors a cool dwarf, a bright white/yellow/blue star means discard
Follow the proper-motion animation (W2 by epoch) to confirm the source walks consistently in one direction year over year, not a static or jumping artifact

Weigh the checklist (proper-motion significance, AllWISE consistency test, Gaia counterpart, W1-W2 color, Pan-STARRS detection) to land on confirm/doubt/discard, using the pipeline's own suggestion only as a cross-check
Track personal accuracy by answer class (confirmed vs discarded) across training rounds to catch bias such as confirming almost everything
Reach a calibrated reviewer level (80% accuracy over the last 20 answers, balanced across answer types) before trusting one's own calls on the real candidate queue

review.summary: The tree correctly frames the training mode as calibrating a reviewer on known-answer brown-dwarf candidates. Its three phases and five features follow the real loop, and almost every cited screen matches its node, with the missing image rendering stated honestly. It needs a few fixes before filing: one wrong screen citation, a missing feature for the example guide, a fuller description of the multi-level proficiency rule, and optionally splitting the oversized evidence-and-checklist feature.
